waypoints.title: ⊕SEGMENTCHAR-ADOPT (:4419) — a shipped surface instantiates templates/SegmentChar.qml rather than drawing segments in its own idiom. The most load-bearing residue: SegmentChar is the one place bloom/weight/pitch could reach every segment surface at once (clock, live wallpaper, splash), instead of each carrying its own. Measure first: what SegmentChar.qml exposes today vs what clock-main.qml draws (strokeLit/strokeGhost, bloom MultiEffect, digitGap/pitch); the gap is the port
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Port step (1)+(2) into templates/SegmentChar.qml ONLY (no surface adopts yet): properties weight (default 1.0), ghostWeight (0.81), bloom (1.5), strokeBase derived from the module (metrics: stroke/1.25 of the cell like make_clock._metrics_holes — pass as a hole or derive from u); litHalf = u*strokeBase*(1+0.25*weight)/2, ghostHalf = u*strokeBase*ghostWeight/2; REPLACE the wider-copy underlay with a lit-only layer under MultiEffect blur (blurMax = litHalf*4*bloom, opacity 0.75, layer.enabled: bloom > 0); rounded ends optional. Then: check_symbol's _bloom_is_blur/_stroke_ratio gain a SegmentChar read (both templates must satisfy), rm + capture_baseline make_segment_display segment_char_component SegmentChar.qml, qml_sanity, and a headless render of the component alone if render_qml has (or gains) a harness for it. Commit; the clock's adoption is the step after.

waypoints.title: ONE THEME, VARIANT SELECTABLE (operator 2026-09-22): collapse the six-of-everything into one set of packages that read the ACTIVE EL colour scheme at runtime — the clock, marquee, live wallpaper, switcher and LnF become one each; variant selection = applying a colour scheme (the .colors files stay six, that is how Plasma variants work). Design first: which solved tokens are reachable live from QML (Kirigami.Theme standard roles: highlight/text/background… — the palette solves fg/fg_in/view/hover/sel into those roles) and which are NOT (the [EL] group: ghost_alpha, ghost_alpha_glanced — a KConfig read the QML cannot do directly; options: bake ghost alpha into a standard-role relation, or ship a tiny helper, or read via a Plasma DataSource); what the gates become when colours are no longer in the emitted bytes (check_ghost_surfaces reads holes today; parity baselines lose the per-variant pairs)
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Measure: a table of every colour hole each surface template fills (lit/ghost/ground/hot/ghostAlpha… via check_ghost_surfaces --map and the  in templates/) against the standard KColorScheme roles the palette writes them into in make_schemes (which token lands in which [Colors:*] role) — the MAPPING decides whether a surface can go live. Then a proof of concept on the switcher (smallest surface): Kirigami.Theme.* in place of the four holes, ONE package, and does it follow plasma-apply-colorscheme EL-Azure -> EL-Amber without reinstall (render_qml cannot see the live scheme; this is a ⊕VER probe). Record in COTYPE as a new symbol with a witness.

waypoints.title: PHOSPHOR CURSORS (operator 2026-09-22: 'isn't the cursor supposed to inherit something related to the color scheme?'): cursors cannot follow the colour scheme by inheritance (fixed images), but the host has /usr/share/icons/breeze_cursors/cursors_scalable/ (SVG sources) — an EL cursor set is a DERIVATION: recolour the SVGs from the palette (lit for the arrow fill? ground for the outline?) and build with xcursorgen per size. Cheap to measure first: how many SVGs, which colours they use (a census), whether xcursorgen is installed (x11-apps/xcursorgen)
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Census only: count the SVGs in cursors_scalable, the distinct fill/stroke colours across them (an SVG colour census tool — check_chrome/check_windows style, or a small mode on check_inherit), and whether xcursorgen exists here; record; decide fill/outline mapping from the palette relation (the arrow must read on BOTH grounds it crosses — a cursor is a glanced-at surface over unknown ground, so it needs an outline, i.e. two tokens).

waypoints.title: PLASMA 6.7 LEGACY THEMES — named (announcement, 2026-06): OXYGEN (KDE 4's default: kstyle + kdecoration + Plasma Style + icons/cursors/sounds) and AIR (the light Plasma Style), 'brought up to par with Breeze' with light/dark/twilight Global Themes, plus the Air and Horos wallpapers; UNION ships as a tech preview (W14 already emits six Union styles — installed, not active here). Theming 'over' Oxygen = a second LnF flavour per variant naming Oxygen's engines (widgetStyle=Oxygen, kwin library org.kde.oxygen) — both read KColorScheme, so the EL scheme already colours them — plus a MEASUREMENT of the Oxygen/Air Plasma Styles: do they follow the system scheme (a colors file / FollowsColorScheme in their metadata) or bake their own?
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Measure on the host: is kde-plasma/oxygen installed (ls /usr/share/plasma/desktoptheme/ for oxygen + air; the Oxygen kstyle plugin; /usr/share/plasma/look-and-feel/ for org.kde.oxygen*); Read oxygen's desktoptheme metadata.json and whether a colors file exists beside it (a Plasma Style without one follows the system scheme; with one, its colours are fixed); Read a stock org.kde.oxygen LnF defaults to see exactly which engines it names. Then decide: an engine=oxygen flavour of build_lnf_packages (six more LnFs — or, if W35 lands, one LnF with an engine choice) and whether make_plasma should emit an Oxygen-shaped Plasma Style (only if Oxygen's bakes colours).

waypoints.title: MARQUEE RING BUFFER (operator live 2026-09-22: with watch notify-send hi the scrolling text blips in and out with the popups). Cause, from templates/marquee-main.qml: rebuild() replaces root.tickerText on every notifModel onCountChanged, so the Repeater tears the Row down mid-scroll. Design (operator): double-buffered rings — the SCROLLING ring loops as long as its notifications are active; a PENDING ring collects arrivals; the swap happens at a full rotation (the NumberAnimation's loop boundary), never mid-scroll; a notification that left the model is dropped at the boundary too
waypoints.evidence: 54fdbe8: tickerText/pendingText + swapRing at the rotation's onFinished (loops: 1, restart), idle swaps immediately; lint clean; parity re-captured; witness pins; COTYPE s91. Live confirmation after re-emerge is the operator's.

waypoints.title: HTML NOTIFICATION BODIES (operator 2026-09-22): some senders emit HTML bodies; parse the markup and let styling drive the dots — bold/strong as lit weight or glow, font color / span color as a HUE on the lit token where the palette allows (a relation gated by the same floors, never a raw literal on the phosphor), i/em perhaps as a slant or ghost weight. CENSUS FIRST: what markup actually arrives (Plasma's notification spec allows b i u a img; senders also emit font color and span style)
waypoints.next_bounded_step: The styling half, in this order: (1) make_palette.rehue(fg, hue) — a GATED re-hue (fg's lightness+chroma at the sender's hue, judged by the lit-vs-ground / lit-vs-ghost / CVD floors, fallback fg) with a selftest arm that a hue failing a floor returns fg; (2) fix the run offsets (collapse whitespace BEFORE run construction, or map indices); (3) MatrixChar gains a per-char lit colour + glow property, the marquee's Repeater reads the run at each index (bold -> glow up by the weight ratio; colour -> rehue result — but the re-hue must be solved at BUILD time per (variant, hue bucket) since the widget carries no colour arithmetic: emit a small hue->lit table into the registry, 12 hue buckets, and the QML looks up); (4) check_ghost_surfaces still finds fg; a harness case for a coloured run. Take (1)+(2) as one tick.
